ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Transaction Reports Act (FTRA), Act No. 17117, as amended; Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment, Act No. 17481; Presidential Enforcement Decree on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; and relevant Supreme Court Registry filings requiring beneficial ownership disclosure to the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KFIU) and the Korea Exchange for UBO verification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention states; Consular Legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate for non-Apostille Convention states. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution appointing the initial representative and granting Power of Attorney

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent local registry (e.g., Seoul Municipal Court or Ministry of Foreign Affairs) for Apostille states; Consular Legalization by Korean diplomatic mission for non-Apostille states. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public or certified corporate counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention member states; Consular Legalization by the Korean Embassy/Consulate in the destination non-member state. No chain sequence is recognized.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean commercial bank (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Compliance officer of the issuing bank, containing KYC verification details
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the bank's designated notary and then Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille states; Consular Legalization by the Korean diplomatic/consular post for non-Apostille states. Only one authentication regime applies based on the destination's treaty membership.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration Form (BEN-1 equivalent per Korean FIU instructions)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: KGID (Korea International Trade Association) or the designated AML supervisory authority when required by banking counterparties
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille states; Consular Legalization for non-member states. Neither apostille nor consular legalization shall be cumulative.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The company must conduct mandatory real-time screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders, signatories and high-risk third parties against: the Korean government's sanctions list under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) recommendations; the UN Security Council Consolidated List; the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List; the European Union consolidated sanctions list; the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) related designations; and the local regulatory watchlists maintained by the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS). For each counterparty, the compliance officer must run a risk score, including Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined under Korea's AML guidelines, and escalate any match to the KFIU before any transaction. The screening must be repapered in clear English, referencing the exact screening result, date, and IP address of the search, and must be re-run no more than 30 days before any corporate bank account opening or equity injection. Any unresolved match terminates the onboarding unless written approval is received from the Governor of the Financial Supervisory Service or the head of the KFIU, as appropriate.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun: All documents originating from jurisdictions that are contracting parties to the Hague Apostille Convention shall receive a single apostille certificate from the competent national authority of the issuing state. For jurisdictions not party to the Convention, the documents shall receive consular legalization from that country's own Ministry of Foreign Affairs or embassy. The two regimes are parallel, mutually exclusive, and shall never be combined or chained sequentially.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court e-Registry (i-SAF) and the Korea Business Information System (KIS) official company name search portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean company names must be registered in Hangul. An original foreign name may be written in Latin characters on the company seal and bank account, but the statutory register must include a Hangul transliteration. The four-tier naming convention requires (i) a distinctive element distinguishing the company from existing registered names, (ii) a business objective phrase describing the actual manufacturing or trading scope, (iii) the corporate liability suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' for limited liability, and (iv) an optional nationwide geographic indicator such as 'Seoul' if desired. The name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to any existing Korean registered company, foreign corporation doing business in Korea, or registered trademark in the same industry. All transliterations from Roman script must faithfully follow the Revised Romanization of Korean (RR) system, and the applicant must obtain a written name clearance certificate from the registry before submitting incorporation documents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: When a name is rejected by the registry examiner on any ground, the applicant must first request a written reason and review the statutory basis under the Commercial Act and the Registration of Commercial Names Regulation. Within 14 days of receiving the rejection notice, the applicant may submit a written appeal to the Commercial Registration Appeals Committee of the relevant district court, attaching a revised name and a corrected transliteration doctrine explanation. If the rejection was based on a confusingly similar existing mark, the applicant shall attach a trademark search report from the Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO) and a declaration of non-confusion. The registry shall issue a decision within 30 days, and if the appeal is denied, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit within 90 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a limited liability company whose industrial activity is high-precision plastic injection molding (ISIC 3240), a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable. The National Tax Service requires a fixed place of business capable of storing production records and issuing tax receipts. Korean banks will also reject a virtual office as the sole qualified registered address due to the inability to conduct physical due diligence. A coworking suite with a dedicated private unit, separate louvred entrance, and documented equipment storage is conditionally acceptable, but must be supplemented with local sublease evidence, a floor plan, and a certificate of actual utility use. The municipal fire commission will require an annual inspection approval. Thus, virtual office is admissible only as a transitional arrangement, and the company must lease a physical factory or workspace within 90 days of incorporation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical on-site inspections are likely to occur with a quantified risk of 65% within the first 24 months for a manufacturing entity claiming factory status. The National Tax Service conducts random tax invoice verification visits on new enterprises with a probability of around 25% in the first year. Municipal environmental and fire safety authorities typically schedule one announced and one unannounced inspection per year. If the registered office is in a commercial building rather than a real factory, the inspection risk rises to 85%. Inspectors shall verify the presence of raw materials, machinery, employee records, and the registered company signboard. Prepare a checklist including the company name board, business license, corporate seal, minute book, quality control system, and fire extinguishers. Absence of any required physical asset may result in fines and suspension of VAT registration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 5052, as finally amended), Chapter 5 (Articles 287-2 through 287-74) on the limited liability company, especially Articles 287-2, 287-9, 287-16, 287-17, 287-25, 287-35, 287-37, and 543; Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 5559, as amended) for non-resident members; Supreme Court Corporate Registration Regulations and the National Tax Service Business Registration Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the Local District Court in the jurisdiction of the registered office; the corporate tax and business registration functions are administered by the National Tax Service District Tax Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation Registration Application (designated registration form for a limited liability company) filed together with the certified Articles of Incorporation, contribution payment certificate, director consent documents, and registered office evidence.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No paid-up capital floor. The Korean Commercial Act does not require a minimum capital for a Yuhan Hoesa, and no national escrow account is mandated. If the articles set a stated capital, the capital must be fully subscribed and effectively paid before the court registration. Non-resident founders generally pay through a foreign-investment account, and the Korean bank issues a contribution receipt; banks may require AML source-of-funds documentation and may hold the funds in a restricted transactional account until business registration is complete.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHANG HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN PLACE OF THE FORMAL ORGANIZATIONAL MEETING

WHEREAS, Yuhan Hoesa is organized as a limited liability company under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, and its Articles of Incorporation are to be filed with the competent Local District Court Registration Office;

WHEREAS, the Articles of Incorporation provide for authorized capital units, the initial members have subscribed for the entire issued capital, and the directors named in the Charter have accepted their offices;

WHEREAS, the directors are required to complete the statutory formation by verifying capital contributions, adopting a registered office, opening corporate banking accounts, and obtaining all industrial and physical licensing;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, AS FOLLOWS:

1. Capital Subscription and Contribution. The Board confirms that the members have subscribed to the issued capital units in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation. The Corporate Representative shall verify payment in full into a corporate account, and the paid amount shall be used exclusively for corporate purposes.

2. Banking Authorization. The Corporate Representative and the Chief Financial Officer, acting singly for payments not exceeding USD 50,000 and jointly for any payment exceeding USD 50,000, are authorized to open and operate corporate settlement and foreign-currency accounts, issue and receive SWIFT wire transfers, sign payment instructions, appoint online banking administrators, and establish PayPal and other low-risk payment rail connections.

3. Registered Office. The registered office and legal domicile of the company shall be the address set out in the Articles of Incorporation. The Corporate Representative is authorized to execute the office and factory lease contracts, register the address with the court and the National Tax Service, and manage all physical facility designations.

4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The Board appoints the individuals identified in the first schedule as Managing Director and Corporate Representative, Chief Financial Officer, Compliance Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each for a term continuing until the next general meeting of members.

5. Corporate Seal and Records. The Corporate Secretary shall procure and register the corporate seal, maintain the registry of members, the minutes book, the members ledger, and all statutory records, and file the seal registration with the District Court.

6. Industrial and Physical Licensing. The Board directs management to execute the Stage 2 licensing plan, including factory establishment approval, environmental prior-review or full EIA to the extent applicable, fire safety and civil defense clearances, and occupational safety approvals before any manufacturing operation begins.

7. Delegation. Each statutory officer is delegated full authority to execute documents, appear before government authorities, retain qualified accountants and attorneys, and take all acts reasonably necessary to complete the formation and licensure.

8. Effectiveness. This resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in force until revoked or amended by the Board. Dated this [date] day of [month], [year].

[Name], Managing Director and Corporate Representative
[Name], Corporate Secretary

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Drafting of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea electronic corporate registration portal and Commercial Registration Division of the Local District Court.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Supreme Court of Korea electronic registration portal to perform a company name search and reservation, or apply through a certified judicial scrivener at the local district court. The proposed name must not be identical to an existing company in the same or similar business. After the name is cleared, prepare the Articles of Incorporation in a notarial form; the purpose clause must expressly cover high-precision steel injection molding of color snap-fit plastic kits, assembly, painting, packaging, distribution, and hobby product export. The charter must state the corporate name, principal office address, issued capital units, amount paid per unit, name and passport data of each member and director, term of office, and the method of publishing financial statements. Execute a professional lease agreement or legal domicile consent for the registered office. If any member is non-resident, the foreign investment notification must be prepared before execution.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of ID or passport of each founding member
Power of attorney if an agent is used
Proposed Articles of Incorporation in three originals
Proof of registered office address, being a lease agreement and owner consent
Statement of capital subscription by each member
Foreign investment notification form if non-resident members are present
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, immediately reserve two alternative names online; if the purpose clause is amended by court pre-examination, narrow it to the exact manufacturing wording and file a corrected charter with unanimous member consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of the proposed registered office under the Law for Notaries and Making of Registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a notary public in the jurisdiction of the proposed registered office with all founders or legal proxies. Each founder shall acknowledge executing the articles and confirm the subscription amount, the number of capital units, and the initial directors. The notary certifies the date, names, signatures, and capacity of each party. For corporate formation purposes, the notarized articles are the principal instrument; the court will not accept unsigned or unattested copies. Ensure at least three original notarized counterparts: one for submission to the registration court, one for the corporate minute book, and one for banking. The notary will also certify the minutes or unanimous written consent if the founders wish to pre-adopt the first board resolution at the same date. The relevant fees are paid to the notary.
required_dossiers: Draft articles in final form
Valid identification or passports of all members
Corporate name reservation confirmation
Capital contribution payment receipt if any pre-deposit has been made
Notarization fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is suspended due to a missing ID or signature, cure by obtaining apostilled identity and special power of attorney for each absent founder and reschedule within two business days; if the notary identifies factual discrepancies, correct by addendum rather than erasure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registration of the Yuhan Hoesa
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the competent Local District Court, using the Supreme Court electronic corporate registration window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation dossier to the commercial registration section of the competent local district court, in person or through the electronic corporate registration portal. The court runs an ex officio legality review of the charter, capital, purpose, director appointments, and statutory form. If compliant, the court enters the company into the Corporate Registry, issues the certificate of registered matters and an original corporate seal certificate, and returns a certified copy to the representative. The statutory registration should be completed within three weeks of notarization; late filing may subject the company to a non-compliance penalty. The application must be signed and sealed by the corporate representative or a proxy holding a notarized power of attorney.
required_dossiers: Application for incorporation registration in court form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of contribution payment issued by the bank
Consent to appointment signed by each director
Registered office lease and landlord consent
Subscription statement of each member
Corporate seal imprint certificate if the seal is registered at the same time
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order, respond within the stated period using the court electronic supplement function; if registration is rejected for nonpayment, pay the registration tax and resubmit with the receipt; if contribution proof is missing, deposit the unpaid amount into the company account and resubmit a fresh payment certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service District Tax Office designated by the registered office jurisdiction, Business Registration and Corporate Tax Unit, through Hometax.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days after court incorporation, apply for the business registration certificate using Hometax or at the local District Tax Office. The business type should be classified as the manufacturing of games and toys, injection molding and assembly, under ISIC 3240 and NAICS 339930. Complete the corporate tax registration, electronic tax invoice issuance, active business site registration, and VAT registration. The National Tax Service reviews the address, corporate seal, and representative identification. On approval, the NTS issues the certificate of business registration, a business number, and the tax invoice login credentials. This certificate is a prerequisite for opening corporate bank accounts, obtaining factory establishment permission, and applying for VAT refunds on imported molds and raw materials.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters issued by the court
Corporate seal certificate
Business registration application form
Registered office and factory lease contract
Identification of the corporate representative
Bank account opening certificate if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS queries the classification, submit a business description and process flow chart using ISIC 3240 and NAICS 339930; if the District Tax Office insists on an on-site visit, complete the protective business evidence and request a re-inspection; if registration is pended due to unpaid municipal tax, pay the imposed local tax surcharge and obtain a zero-tax due certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation and Post-Formation Regulatory and Labor Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Banking Department of a licensed commercial bank and the four-insurance integrated portal operated by the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Employment Insurance Office, and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the corporate settlement account and a foreign currency account at the bank chosen under the board resolution. Presentation of the court certificate, business registration certificate, corporate seal, seal certificate, and representative passport. The bank performs beneficial ownership, AML, and source-of-funds review. After approval, configure SWIFT wire, corporate online banking, PayPal business setup for hobbyist orders, and any foreign exchange trading standard permissions. Thereafter, register the company and all initial employees with the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Employment Insurance Office, and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Office using the four-insurance integrated portal. Obtain a workplace registration number for the factory and attach the hazardous machine inventory and material safety data sheets for the injection molding presses.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters
Certificate of Business Registration
Corporate seal certificate and seal imprint
Identification of the corporate representative and beneficial owner declaration
Evidence of paid-in capital remittance
Articles of Incorporation
Directory of initial employees and compensation schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank onboarding is delayed by AML review, provide the complete source of funds, a side letter on beneficial ownership, and a notarized board resolution; if the four-insurance portal does not recognize the new corporate business number, obtain the NTS certificate and request manual registration at the local insurance branch; any workplace injury insurance registration gap caused by administrative delay can be cured by retroactive premium payment without loss of accident coverage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of SMEs and Startups, local Metropolitan or Provincial Government one-stop business support center, Korea Industrial Complex Corporation, Ministry of Environment, National Fire Agency, and Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Establishment Approval and Registration Certificate under the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act; the related manufacturing

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online portal HomeTax at hometax.go.kr; export customs clearance is administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS single-window portal at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa is organized as a Korean domestic corporation and must register as a business operator with the NTS before commencing taxable activity. The non-resident shareholders appoint a domestic tax representative if no Korean office is open. Within 20 days of commencing business, the company files an Application for Business Registration and the corporate facts-of-establishment form with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the company's Korean head office, attaching: certificate of incorporation, Korean commercial registry certificate, articles of association, board resolution on foreign investment, financial institution account opening confirmation, and the tax representative's power of attorney. After review, the NTS issues the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) which functions as the VAT ID and corporate income tax TIN. A foreign non-resident supplier with no Korean place of business but Korean VAT liability uses the HomeTax simplified registration procedure for foreign suppliers of electronic services and obtains a BRN for VAT purposes; the same BRN is used for VAT returns and zero-rating claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea has no check-the-box or hybrid entity election. A Yuhan Hoesa is automatically classified as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and is taxed on its worldwide income at the entity level; no pass-through election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary registration threshold. Registration is mandatory from the first taxable supply by any business operator in Korea. A simplified taxable person regime for eligible small businesses with prior-calendar-year turnover below KRW 80 million reduces VAT administration but does not postpone or waive registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory for VAT-registered businesses and must be transmitted to the NTS through HomeTax or an NTS-approved e-document provider by the day after issuance; Korean tax invoices issued to B2B users require an NTS issuance record. There is no separate pre-clearance physical fiscal stamp; the anti-fraud control is the NTS e-tax invoice database, mandatory UNI-PASS customs declaration, bank foreign-exchange settlement matching, and automated cross-referencing of export zero-rating evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, the export of goods manufactured by the Korean entity is zero-rated if the goods are the subject of an accepted customs export declaration with the Korean company as exporter of record, the goods physically depart the Republic of Korea, the export sale is reported as zero-rated on the NTS VAT return, and the exporter retains the documentary trail: accepted UNI-PASS export declaration, shipping documents, invoice/packing list, and proof of receipt of foreign currency from the non-resident buyer. Offshore digital services supplied to a non-resident for use outside Korea are also zero-rated if the place-of-supply rules and NTS non-resident evidence requirements are satisfied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Accepted Export Declaration (Export Permit) issued through KCS UNI-PASS
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing departure from Korea

Foreign exchange bank Export Proceeds Receipt Certificate or Foreign Exchange Transaction Certificate (the Korean FIRC equivalent), supported by SWIFT credit advice/PayPal settlement report identifying the non-resident remitter and the credit to the Korean entity's bank account
Zero-rated e-tax invoice record (if an invoice is issued for the export transaction)
Finished-goods inventory and purchase/input VAT dockets for input credit substantiation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS may deny zero-rating and claw back any refunded input VAT if any export document is missing, inconsistent, or fraudulent. Disallowed zero-rating results in output VAT at 10% being assessed on the supply value, plus statutory interest and VAT additional taxes for incorrect reporting or false tax invoices (generally 2% of the supply value for omitted/falsely entered sales). Aggravated cases are referred under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with criminal fines/imprisonment possible. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days without a permitted extension also exposes the exporter to administrative penalties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and may invalidate the zero-rate claim for that shipment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting through the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act framework; the Ministry of Economy and Finance exercises overall foreign exchange policy supervision, and all licensed foreign exchange banks file reporting through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized current account regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with the Bank of Korea and the Ministry of Economy and Finance exercising prudential oversight through the Foreign Exchange Information System. For export and import commercial settlements, payments and receipts clear without individual central bank approval, but banking channels require a transaction declaration for each remittance exceeding the statutory basket, especially for capital-account flows. Capital account transactions have been progressively liberalized and are generally handled through notification or reporting to the designated foreign exchange bank rather than requiring central bank prior approval. Inbound foreign direct investment must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before or immediately after the capital is wired, and the proceeds must be parked in a named foreign-investment deposit account until capital verification is completed. Profit remittances such as dividends and retained-earning distributions are current-account payments; they are technically freely convertible, but the paying bank will demand evidence of the dividend approval, audited financial statements, tax clearance, and the investor's shareholding record. Export receipts do not have to be compulsorily sold to the central bank; the exporter can hold foreign currency in a domestic foreign-exchange bank account, but settlement and collection deadlines must be met and the inflow must be reported through FEIS. Any conversion to KRW is executed at the prevailing market exchange rate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export claims must be collected and settled within the payment term stated in the underlying export sales contract, generally no later than 180 days from the date of export unless the responsible foreign exchange bank extends the deadline for documented open-account, deferred-payment or overseas consignment arrangements. There is no mandatory KRW conversion ratio for export proceeds; the effective surrender ratio is 0%, meaning the exporter may retain all foreign currency receipts in a Foreign Currency Deposit Account with a licensed foreign exchange bank or sell them to that bank at the market rate. The proceeds must be credited to a domestic foreign exchange account held by the Korean entity and the receipt must be reported through the Foreign Exchange Information System, cross-matching the exporter's customs declaration, invoice, and bank credit. Failure to settle within the approved timeline exposes the entity to fines, collection orders, and administrative impediments to future trade payments.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Capital Deposit Account for initial inbound equity escrow plus KRW operating account
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW) and Foreign Currency Settlement Account (USD/EUR/JPY)
Corporate Treasury Clearing Account with multi-currency functionality for trade settlements
Basic Operational Currency Account and dedicated FX hedging account for forward contracts

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability and materially restricted. Offshore digital EMI platforms are not licensed banks or authorized electronic financial companies in South Korea and cannot hold KRW corporate deposits or provide local clearing membership. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, an unlicensed non-bank entity accepting Korean corporate funds would expose the treasury relationship to adverse regulatory findings. A cross-border EMI may be used only indirectly, if at all, as a payment hook for overseas e-commerce receipts through licensed money transmitter partnerships, but it cannot serve as the primary liquidity or clearing rail. The Yuhan Hoesa should open all corporate clearing and escrow relationships with a domestic tier-1 licensed commercial bank and maintain PayPal/Swift wire as receivables channels only.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company, the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and FATF-aligned AML obligations require the legal entity's director, authorized signatory, and each beneficial owner to complete the bank's customer risk-identification procedure. Most tier-1 Korean banks require at least one registered statutory director to appear physically in-branch to sign account-opening documents and undergo the compliance interview, especially where non-resident ownership is present or initial capital is introduced by a foreign remitter. Remote consular proxy opening is not a standard service; a few banks may allow a domestic attorney-in-fact to complete the branch visit under a notarized power-of-attorney that is additionally apostilled or consular-certified, but the bank's approval committee will still require video identification of the director and may insist that the director appear personally before the account can be activated. Documents must be certified as true copies and refreshed within three months of submission.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder wealth origin and lack of a Korean tax or credit footprint, making source-of-funds verification difficult.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies and proof of residency for every individual UBO; two years of personal/corporate tax returns; audited global financial statements or bank reference letters from the remitting institution; a written source-of-wealth declaration; and bank statements showing the source account used for the capital injection, with the FX wire field indicating direct investment equity and the foreign investment notification number.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential trade invoice mismatch for high-priced action-figure and mecha kit exports, including risk of over- or under-invoicing through related-party distributors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Korea Customs Service export declarations and matched invoices; signed commercial sales contracts with distribution terms; HS code classifications and product catalogues showing reasonable unit economics; packing lists and air/sea waybills; PayPal or marketplace settlement statements; and, if related parties are involved, transfer pricing documentation or an advance pricing arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Execution of bulk low-value cross-border payments through PayPal and online hobby-marketplace rails, which can be confused with third-party settlement or unsanctioned money remittance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform merchant agreements and valid customer contracts; monthly PayPal/MPU settlement reports; chargeback and refund policies; a clear description of the marketplace sales pipeline from preorder to fulfillment; a sanctions-screening and end-user compliance statement; and an undertaking that no third-party pass-through clearing will be performed on the corporate account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office is a virtual office or shared commercial address, with no verified operational manufacturing or warehousing presence in South Korea.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized lease agreement or utility bill in the company's name; corporate registration certificate with current address; invitation for the bank to conduct a physical on-site inspection; photographs of the production/storage facilities; and an organisational chart showing employees or outsourcing contracts supporting the injection-molding and hobby-kit assembly business described by ISIC 3240.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The overseas parent or shareholder must remit via SWIFT MT103 to the bank account opened in the Yuhan Hoesa's name, using a purpose classification in the FEIS declaration that covers direct investment equity. The remitter field must match the registered foreign investor, and the payment detail field should carry the investor's foreign investment notification or registration number so the Korean bank can verify the FDI entry. Funds should be routed through a licensed foreign exchange bank to the designated Foreign Investment Capital Deposit Account, where the bank performs capital verification before the sums are permitted to be transferred into the operational KRW account or used for permitted business expenses. The bank will record the inward remittance, convert at the applicable market rate if a KRW injection is required, and file the transaction with FEIS under the Korean balance-of-payments classification. No final capital conversion is permitted before the bank confirms the foreign investment report and the capital verification process.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Export-related and import-related trade payments should be settled through the licensed Korean bank's foreign-currency settlement rail. For normal distributor settlements and goods purchases, execute SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers with the correct BOK/FEIS transaction classification for merchandise trade and attach the customs declaration evidence in bank files. For higher-value raw material procurement of resins, paints, and precision moulds, a commercial irrevocable letter of credit governed by UCP 600 can be opened via SWIFT MT700, with the Korean bank advising and confirming structure chosen by the beneficiary. Documentary collections (D/P and D/A) are acceptable for mid-tier suppliers using banking channels that transmit drafts, invoices, bills of lading, insurance certificates, and customs outbound declarations. All outbound payments require the original or scanned commercial invoice, packing list, export declaration, and end-user documentation where product sensitivity warrants.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable KRW/USD forward contracts with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank, supported by confirmed trade receivables or payables and filed through FEIS as a current-trade hedge.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed through an authorized Korean or international bank only when an actual or contingent KRW exposure exists and the instrument is documented as a hedge; speculative NDF trading is prohibited.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps or foreign currency swaps used to re-align debt and revenue currency for a foreign-invested enterprise, subject to bank counterparty approval and an underlying exposure report.
Short-dated FX collar or plain-vanilla option structures purchased as a protection overlay against adverse moves on committed trade flows, with no net option-income generation or uncovered writing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporation income tax return and attached financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS) via HomeTax electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March of the following tax year for a company with a 31 December fiscal year end; extendable to 31 May after filing an extension request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Understatement penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax amount; non-filing penalty of 40% of the unpaid amount; late-payment interest accrues daily at 0.025% (approximately 9.21% per annum); persistent default allows the NTS to seize bank accounts, cancel the business registration with the local tax office, and initiate criminal prosecution for wilful tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual report on the foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) and Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the preceding calendar year; must cover the calendar period 1 January to 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative coercion fine of up to KRW 5 million (USD 3,800) under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; failure to file may cause revocation of the foreign-invested enterprise designation, retroactive clawback of tax and customs incentives, and a formal demand to remedy the non-compliance; continued omission can lead to an order for administrative strike-off from the FDI support list.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report and certified financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service; filing with the Financial Supervisory Service (DART) is required only for public-interest and listed-group entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days from the fiscal year end for a private Yuhan Hoesa; a 31 December year-end therefore requires submission by 31 March; if the regular general meeting of members approves the financial statements at a later date, the report must be filed within 14 days after that approval but no later than 120 days after the year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file an audit report with the NTS attracts an administrative fine of up to KRW 30 million (USD 22,800) under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; the auditor and responsible management may also receive a disciplinary sanction imposed by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants; non-audit does not by itself trigger commercial strike-off but will cause the corporate tax return to be treated as materially incomplete, leading to a full tax inquiry and blocked director credit records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minutes of the regular general meeting of members and updated statutory member register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's registered office in Korea (internal statutory record with no government filing fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The regular general meeting of members must be convened within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December fiscal year end the meeting is required by 31 March; the register must be continuously maintained and updated by the date of each transfer or capital change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain the member register or to convene the regular meeting may trigger an administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million (USD 3,800) under Article 635 of the Korean Commercial Act; minority members may petition the court for an order to convene a meeting; repeated contravention will expose the business managers to civil liability for damages and can be treated by the Commercial Registry as a serious governance deficiency.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (enforced by Presidential Decree), an independent certified CPA audit is mandated for a non-listed Yuhan Hoesa when any of the following quantitative criteria is met at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year: (a) balance-sheet total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (USD 9.1 million); (b) total assets equal or exceed KRW 7 billion and the company has a debt-to-equity ratio higher than 100% at the balance-sheet date and has obtained a bank loan of more than KRW 5 billion during the fiscal year; (c) the company has 100 or more permanent manufacturing or administrative employees in addition to total assets exceeding KRW 8 billion; or (d) consolidated-year turnover exceeds KRW 30 billion where the company is the designated anchor entity of a corporate group subject to the external audit law. Any foreign-invested enterprise with total assets above KRW 5 billion that has been specifically directed by the Minister of Strategy and Finance due to public interest or investor protection is also required to undergo an audit; all such thresholds are reviewed annually by the Korean Accounting Standards Board and the Financial Supervisory Service.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: A statutory audit must be conducted pursuant to Korean Accounting Standards (K-GAAP) for a standard Yuhan Hoesa, with the option to adopt Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) if the company is a public-interest entity, an entity designated for external audit by the Financial Supervisory Service, or if it has elected to adopt K-IFRS voluntarily. Eligible small companies may use the Korean SME Accounting Standards, but all audited companies must reconcile to the qualitative and quantitative requirements of the Korean Financial Accounting Standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not operate a stand-alone annual beneficial-ownership register for private LLCs; however, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act mandates an annual report of ultimate beneficial owners and foreign investor holdings filing to MOTIE/KOTRA by 31 March. In addition, the Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act requires all account-opening documents to identify natural-person beneficial owners whenever a new finance relationship is established, and any change to a member's interest must be evidenced in minutes and reflected in the member ledger. A transfer of a membership interest in a Yuhan Hoesa requires the consent of all other members unless the articles of incorporation expressly permit transfer; after the transfer the entity must file a change of corporate registration with the local Commercial Registry within 30 days and update the statutory register immediately, failing which an administrative fine up to KRW 5 million (USD 3,800) may be imposed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Business Managers (equivalent to the register of directors in a stock company)
Register of Charges, Mortgages and Pledges over Membership Interests

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.2% combined effective top marginal corporate rate (22% national Corporate Income Tax plus 10% local income tax surtax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general free-zone patent-box holiday is available for an ordinary Yuhan Hoesa manufacturing action figures; qualifying SMEs may use R&D tax credits, investment/job-creation credits, and foreign dividend income exemption (95%) under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, lowering the effective rate below the statutory headline. The baseline NOL regime in this pipeline is 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Standard Corporate Income Tax Return under Article 60 of the Korean Corporate Income Tax Act, e-filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr); local income tax surtax is filed through the Local Tax E-Filing system (wetax.go.kr) as an integrated corporate-local return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing, with a semi-annual interim corporate tax prepayment due within 2 months after each half-year period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing must be made within 3 months of the fiscal-year end; for a December 31 year-end the statutory deadline is March 31, and one additional month may be granted by the district tax office upon timely request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, fiscal-year basis, business registration number, corporate form, place of effective management, and foreign direct ownership schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean business registration and Foreign Investment Promotion Act registration number if foreign-owned; disclose the ultimate beneficial owner. If the place of effective management is in Korea, the company must report worldwide income; otherwise it must report only Korean-source income and attach a PE analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of book net income to taxable income, including nondeductible expenses, tax-exempt income, and deferred tax timing differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back excess intercompany royalties, management fees, or interest paid to nonresident related parties that fail the arm's-length standard, and exclude qualified foreign-source dividends if the 95% dividend exemption is claimed. Attach all adjustment schedules under the Corporate Income Tax Act and the International Tax Adjustment Law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable base after prior-year loss carryforward and unabsorbed deficit deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the five-year carryforward recognized by the pipeline; do not carry foreign branch losses into the Korean return. Where DTA rules permit a foreign tax credit for a disregarded overseas payment, the credit must be allocated to the exact Korean-source item and substantiated with a TRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: National Corporate Income Tax computation using the Korean progressive brackets: 10% up to KRW 200 million, 20% up to KRW 20 billion, and 22% above KRW 20 billion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a nonresident controlled Korean entity, recompute the tax base if related-party adjustments are proposed by the National Tax Service. The income attributable to the Korean manufacturing and design functions must reflect the risks assumed by the Yuhan Hoesa and must not be artificially stripped by buy-sell or commission payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and reductions: foreign tax credits, R&D credits, investment tax credits, low-income employment credits, and donations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the foreign tax credit only for foreign withholding taxes legally due and actually paid; attach the NTS foreign tax credit schedule and TRC for each country. The credit is limited to the Korean tax attributable to the foreign-source income; excess credits cannot be carried forward generally.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surtax: 10% of the national Corporate Income Tax amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the surtax on the same adjusted taxable base. A treaty reduction never applies to the Korean local income surtax; only the national CIT withholding can be reduced under a DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of outbound payments to non-residents subject to withholding: dividends, interest, royalties, and other consideration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List every payment to the foreign shareholder or parent. Withhold at 22% (20% national WHT plus 2% local surtax) unless a DTA relief request accompanied by the beneficial owner's TRC and residency certificate has been approved or filed beforehand. Attach proof of beneficial ownership; a conduit company without substance cannot receive reduced rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International tax adjustment and transfer pricing disclosure: related-party transaction schedules, local file, master file, and country-by-country report notification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all intercompany purchases of resins, steel injection molds, digital character licenses, royalty payments, and overseas sales commissions. If aggregate related-party international transactions exceed the statutory threshold, attach the contemporaneous Local and Master File. A tested-party analysis must treat the Korean Yuhan Hoesa as the manufacturer performing design, production, and warranty functions, and should not leave it with no economic substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a surtax up to 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; dishonest underreporting attracts a 40% additional-tax penalty on the understated amount; overdue tax accrues a daily nonpayment surcharge while unpaid, and the National Tax Service may name high-value delinquents, impose departure bans, and refer fraudulent returns for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act with potential imprisonment of up to five years and fines up to ten times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax on nonresident dividends under Article 98 of the Corporate Income Tax Act plus 10% local income tax surtax), reduced where an applicable Korea income tax treaty provides for 5%, 10%, or 15% dividend withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The payee must deliver a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its country of residence, a completed treaty-relief application, and a beneficial ownership declaration to the Korean payer before the payment date. The Korean payer must retain the documents in its withholding records, remit withholding at the reduced treaty rate only if the application is administratively accepted; otherwise it must withhold at the statutory 22% rate and the nonresident may file a timely refund claim to the National Tax Service. Additional substance checks under the OECD Multilateral Instrument Principal Purpose Test may deny the DTA benefit when one of the main purposes of the entity or payment routing is treaty shopping.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on outbound royalty and interest income is 22% combined (20% national plus 2% local surtax). Korean DTAs typically reduce interest to 10% (with 0% for governmental and export-credit bodies in many treaties) and royalties to 10-15% depending on the jurisdiction and the beneficial ownership facts; industrial or copyright royalties usually require TRC and substance proof.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 50 billion in annual aggregate related-party international transactions for the full Local File and Master File; KRW 5 billion for simplified documentation; KRW 1 trillion consolidated group revenue triggers Country-by-Country reporting.
